svg.title: Affine ind-regular completion and the isolated-point retract
svg.desc: On a smooth affine complex chart the operator algebra has finite projective resolutions of coherent modules, not necessarily free last terms. Full compact mapping tests and the derived product-difference formula recover the lower-truncation inverse tower. Within the actual ind-regular category both continuous point adjoints exist. For objects whose cohomology is a filtered union of coherent isolated-carrier objects, their comparison is an equivalence. The right counit and left unit then give an inclusion and retraction with identity composite. The algebraic cycle application retains its bounded carrier and nonzero-test premises. Global stack descent and the microlocal support comparison remain separate.
svg.text: Affine completion and an unbounded isolated-point retract
Actual Ind of bounded regular D-modules on a smooth affine complex chart U.
1. Retain the projective last syzygy — IAC.1–IAC.8
A = D(U), gr A = Sym over O(U) of the derivation module.
Global finite projective operator resolution: length at most 2 dim U.
Compact c in degrees [r,s], arbitrary Z ≤ b:
RHom(c,Z) ≤ b−r. This bound includes unbounded-below targets.
The actual ind-regular embedding has inherited truncations and coherent heart unions.
2. Recover the specified inverse tower — IAC.9–IAC.15
Eₙ = τ ≥−n E, Eₙ₊₁ → Eₙ, fibre(E → Eₙ) = τ ≤−n−1 E.
For each compact c and fixed mapping degree, the fibre bound tends to −∞.
Derived limit = fibre( product Vₙ —1−shift→ product Vₙ ).
Exact vector-space products and eventual stabilization give E ≃ lim Eₙ.
A finite-amplitude continuous extension obeys this tower comparison.
3. Compare both point adjoints in the regular category — IAC.16–IAC.22
At a closed point: i* ⊣ i_* ⊣ i!; all three functors are continuous.
θ_E : i!E → i*E is i* of the right counit, with i* i_* = Id.
Each coherent heart piece: point coefficient ⊕ disjoint closed-carrier part.
For admissible cohomology, finite amplitude reduces each degree to a finite window.
θ_E is an equivalence on an arbitrary unbounded E with those cohomology objects.
No common support neighbourhood and no derived-heart identification are required.
4. The actual maps split the point object — IAC.23–IAC.29
u = right counit : i_* i!E → E
r = i_*(θ_E inverse) · left unit : E → i_* i!E
r u = Id, e = u r, e² = e, E ≃ i_* i!E ⊕ cofib(u).
For the algebraic ind-cycle functor, retain the bounded isolated-carrier premise.
One nonzero bounded point test stays nonzero by the actual heart injection.
5. Scope and explicit counterchecks — IAC.30–IAC.35
Smooth relative dimension r: f! [−r] is the exact normalized inverse transfer.
R = C × C, P = R(1,0): finite projective, but ranks (1,0) forbid freeness.
W ⊗ − obeys the truncation tower and can fail to preserve countable products.
⊕ⱼ (δ₀ ⊕ δ₁⁄₍ⱼ₊₁₎)[j] has the δ₀ retract in every negative degree.
No one Zariski neighbourhood separates all its infinitely many away points.
Global stack truncation/limit descent retains its explicit evaluation hypotheses.
Exact proofs: §§3.289–3.301; IAC.1–IAC.35; Solutions3.EH,3.EI,3.EJ.
The cycle application uses the proved bounded algebraic regular-function scope.
Generic microlocal coefficients and characteristic-support/RH comparison remain separate.
These local results do not establish nilpotent image or full-image regularity.
The point operations above are those of the actual regular ind-category.
